stem: By the end of 1880, almost 50,000 telephones were in use in the United States. What does that rapid spread best show?

stimulus.source_note: Alexander Graham Bell's first transmitted words, March 10, 1876, as recorded in his laboratory notebook and reported by the Smithsonian Institution and the Library of Congress. Public domain.
stimulus.text:
"Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you."

— Alexander Graham Bell, speaking into his experimental telephone to his assistant Thomas Watson, March 10, 1876, three days after Bell received U.S. Patent No. 174,465 for the telephone.

options.text: The telephone failed, since almost no one wanted one
options.misconception: Background: 50,000 telephones in four years is fast growth for a brand-new invention, not failure.

options.text: A new invention could reach everyday business use within a few years
The government bought every telephone and gave them away free
options.misconception: Background: the Bell Telephone Company sold telephones as a business; the government did not buy or give them away.

options.text: The telephone replaced the railroad as the main way to move goods
options.misconception: Background: the telephone moved words, not goods; freight still traveled by rail.

rationales.A: Background: 50,000 telephones within four years of the first call is rapid growth, not failure. A failed invention gathers dust, not customers.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Bell's telephone was patented in 1876, the Bell Telephone Company was established within a year, and by the end of 1880 almost 50,000 telephones were in use. A laboratory device became a business tool in four years.
rationales.C: Background: the Bell Telephone Company was a private business that sold telephone service. The government did not buy the telephones or give them away.
rationales.D: Background: the telephone carried voices, not freight. Goods still moved by rail, and the railroads kept growing.
rationales.general:
Count the years, then count the phones.
1. The first words traveled in March 1876, from one room to the next.
2. Background: by the end of 1880, almost 50,000 telephones were in use across the country.
3. Background: four years took the telephone from an experiment to a business tool.
Remember: speed of spread is the best measure of how much a new tool was wanted.

books.section: The Age of Invention and Economic Growth
